summary: A satirical article dated September 15, 2023 that humorously treats aging utility infrastructure (electricity, water, gas, internet) as a return to medieval living. It uses invented residents and experts to joke about outages, a claimed 87% rise in service interruptions, and the need to appreciate repair crews, and ends with a mock conclusion lost to an outage.
one_line: A humorous 2023 satire on aging electricity, water, gas and internet infrastructure causing outages that force candlelit, medieval-style living.
key_facts: The article is dated September 15, 2023 and satirizes aging infrastructure as a return to medieval living.
Ethel Muckraker, 72, lives in the historic neighbourhood of Copperwire Hollow and says of outages, "You can't tweet warmth."
Dr. Thaddeus Lightbulb, Professor of Antediluvian Engineering at the Old World University, jokes that time travellers are stealing parts of the electrical grid to sell as future antiques.
The article claims service outages are up 87% since the year prior to 2023.
Mildred Splash, a water enthusiast from the Drysdale region, says "If the taps won't flow, I will!" about water outages.
Documents dated February 30th, which officials call a clerical error, reportedly show more surprise no-water days than snow days.
Harold Fuego, a retired firefighter and candle enthusiast, says "I've traded my hose for a fire extinguisher; the flame is closer to home these days."
The gas infrastructure is described as aged like fine wine and as reliable as a weather forecast by Punxsutawney Phil.
An anonymous telecom worker jokes that some people miss dial-up Internet, which had "a certain...je ne sais doom."
Neighborhoods have reinstated the torchbearer profession, and children are introduced to a paper-based 'pre-screen' era.
Emergency service workers and repair crews are called the real MVPs of the outages.
The article ends with a mock 'conclusion' that supposedly succumbed to an outage, and a toast to the 'invisible knights of Utilities'.
